title: Intermediate Densification of Collagen Hydrogels Promotes Fibrocartilage-Like Tendon-Bone Healing.
abstract: Regeneration of the fibrocartilaginous tendon-bone enthesis remains a challenge because scar tissue often replaces the functional transitional interface. Biomaterial scaffolds can provide physical cues for interface regeneration, but conventional collagen hydrogels have sparse fibrillar networks and low stiffness. Here, graded plastic compression co-tuned collagen density, pore area fraction, degradation behavior, and multiscale stiffness within a chemically unchanged collagen I system. The target reductions in initial gel thickness were 0% (non-compressed, NC), 50% (low-compression, LC), 70% (moderate-compression, MC), and 90% (high-compression, HC). Material properties changed progressively across these conditions, whereas bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) responses were non-monotonic. MC was the first condition to show a marked increase in bulk stiffness, with corresponding local stiffening, while remaining less compact than HC; it also produced the most favorable overall proliferation, fibrocartilage-associated marker expression, and matrix deposition among the four conditions tested. RNA sequencing revealed MC-associated transcriptional programs related to the cell cycle, cartilage development, extracellular matrix organization, and candidate mechanosensing processes. Pharmacological FAK inhibition reduced MC-associated FAK phosphorylation, YAP1 nuclear localization, and SOX9 expression without a measurable change in total integrin β1 fluorescence intensity, supporting a FAK-sensitive contribution within the YAP1/SOX9 response. In a rat rotator cuff repair model, the selected MC construct improved gait and mechanical properties and promoted more organized fibrocartilage-like interface remodeling compared with the control conditions. These findings identify an intermediate densification physical window within the tested collagen I series and establish graded compression as a practical strategy for selecting collagen constructs for tendon-bone repair. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Rotator cuff repair rarely restores the fibrocartilaginous tendon-bone interface. Existing biomaterial studies often vary scaffold composition, bioactive signals, and physical properties together, making the contribution of matrix physical state difficult to define. By applying graded plastic compression to a compositionally constant type I collagen system, this study identifies an intermediate densification window that outperforms both minimally and maximally compressed matrices in supporting mesenchymal stem cell proliferation and fibrocartilage-associated differentiation. Transcriptomic profiling and pharmacological inhibition further support a FAK-sensitive contribution to the YAP1/SOX9 response. The selected construct also improves gait, mechanical properties, and interface organization in vivo. These findings reveal a non-monotonic structure-function relationship and provide a broadly relevant physical design principle for regenerative biomaterials and tendon-bone repair.

title: Heterotopic ossification: a comprehensive narrative review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, prevention, and emerging therapies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterotopic ossification is the formation of mature bone in extraskeletal soft tissues after trauma, orthopaedic surgery, burns, or neurological injury.
REVIEW FINDINGS: Pathogenesis involves mesenchymal stem cell differentiation driven by bone morphogenetic protein, transforming growth factor beta, Wnt/beta-catenin, and hypoxia-inducible factor signalling within an inflammatory microenvironment. Ultrasound detects the zone phenomenon approximately two weeks before radiography; magnetic resonance imaging shows striate and checkerboard patterns in pre-calcification lesions. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and low-dose radiation remain effective prophylactic strategies. Physiotherapy is central to conservative management, and extracorporeal shock wave therapy may benefit traumatic cases. Excision is reserved for symptomatic lesions causing significant functional limitation, pain, or neurovascular compromise, ideally after maturation to reduce recurrence, although earlier intervention may be feasible in selected athletes.
CONCLUSION: Palovarotene is the first disease-modifying treatment approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. An individualised, multidisciplinary approach is essential; biomarker research and targeted pharmacotherapy remain priorities.

title: Therapeutic potential of umbilical cord-derived MSCs in arthritis: Insights from preclinical and clinical studies.
abstract: Among different types of arthritis, osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain the most common and primary cause of pain and disability worldwide, characterized by progressive joint degeneration and persistent inflammation. Although there have been developments in pharmacology, the available treatment program slows disease progression and provides only symptomatic relief. However, their ability to repair and restore damaged tissue is limited. This highlights the importance of regenerative therapy in actively modulating the immune system while stimulating tissue regeneration. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed, Scopus, Web of science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ChiCTR, focusing on preclinical and clinical studies of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) therapy in OA and RA. Recently, UC-MSC have been emerging as a promising therapeutic approach due to their immunomodulatory and regenerative properties. Because they are harvested noninvasively, these cells have greater proliferative capacity and lower immunogenicity than MSCs derived from bone marrow or adipose tissue. UC-MSCs do not replace damaged cells; instead, they signal other cells to produce bioactive substances that reduce inflammation and promote cartilage repair. Data from emerging preclinical and clinical trials, which show significant improvements in WOMAC and VAS scores and a decrease in DAS28 with minimal adverse effects, suggest that UC-MSCs will improve pain and function and, in turn, overall quality of life. UC-MSCs represent a mechanistically distinct and clinically promising therapeutic effect for OA and RA, addressing both the inflammatory and degenerative condition of joint disease. However, there are still large, well-designed, standardized clinical trials that can best optimize doses and treatment plans. This narrative review summarizes the various forms of arthritis, disease pathogenesis, and preclinical and clinical evidence for the use of UC-MSCs in the treatment of arthritis, such as OA and RA.

title: From bouts to readiness to compete: temporal dynamics of stress, fatigue, recovery and monitoring-informed decisions in combat sports.
abstract: Combat-sport tournaments require decisions before responses to previous efforts have resolved. Detecting a change does not establish that an indicator predicts the next task or improves a decision. This Perspective proposes a task- and time-specific framework linking prior bouts, recovery time and subsequent demands through three evidentiary requirements. Responsiveness concerns reproducible changes beyond measurement error when an indicator represents a response to effort. Predictive validity concerns anticipation of a pre-specified subsequent outcome and added information beyond simpler measures. Decision utility concerns improved outcomes relative to usual practice. Indicators interpreted as current status or stable capacity need not respond to prior effort, but still require adequate measurement properties and prospective evaluation. Evidence from repeated bouts, recovery interventions, mental fatigue, sleep restriction and weight loss suggests that monitoring domains are not interchangeable. The framework retains discordant indicators, evaluates combinations and communicates uncertainty without global clearance labels. Three hypotheses address task and time dependence, maintained performance with increasing effort cost, and indicator-informed decisions. Medical decisions remain independent and take precedence. This is an operational extension of existing principles, not a validated predictive tool.

title: Sleep Management in Paralympic Sports: Knowledge, Monitoring Practices, and Perceived Barriers among Coaches and Healthcare Staff.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coaches and healthcare staff play a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about the importance of sleep to develop a precise balance between recovery and the demands imposed by sports training.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge on sleep, jet lag, and sleep hygiene (SH) among coaches and healthcare staff in Paralympic sports; 2) to identify whether the sleep of Paralympic athletes is monitored, and which instruments are commonly used; and 3) to identify the main barriers faced in sleep management.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present cross-sectional study was conducted with 60 coaches and healthcare staff who work in the preparation of elite Paralympic athletes. The participants filled out the Sleep Beliefs Scale and a structured questionnaire before traveling to the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games.
RESULTS: Coaches and healthcare staff understand the importance of sleep for sports performance and recovery, but only 56% monitored their sleep. The most commonly used methods were subjective. Lack of adherence and commitment among Paralympic athletes (27%) and lack of training (19%) were the main barriers to sleep management.
CONCLUSION: Coaches and healthcare staff are aware of the importance of sleep; however, educational programs are needed to improve the training of coaching and healthcare staff for efficient sleep management and to raise awareness among Paralympic athletes about the importance of sleep.

title: Electrospun scaffolds for MSC-derived secretome delivery.
abstract: The mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC)-derived secretome is emerging as a promising cell-free therapeutic product for tissue repair and regeneration. It contains soluble proteins, growth factors, nucleic acids, and extracellular vesicles (EVs), whose combined activity supports angiogenesis, immunomodulation, cytoprotection, and extracellular matrix remodelling. However, the biological activity of these components can be compromised during processing, storage, scaffold loading, and release. This review examines electrospun scaffolds as delivery platforms for the MSC-derived secretome, with particular attention to EV preservation and analytical evaluation. Selected non-electrospun platforms are discussed as comparators to clarify the advantages and limitations of electrospun delivery systems. We discuss how polymer composition, solvent exposure, crosslinking, fibre architecture, and loading strategy affect cargo retention, release kinetics, and biological activity. Post-fabrication adsorption generally minimises processing-related exposure of labile components but often results in rapid release, whereas matrix incorporation, affinity-based immobilisation, and microsphere-assisted loading can prolong delivery while introducing additional risks to vesicle and protein stability. Preclinical studies across these scaffold platforms report beneficial effects in models of skin, bone, cartilage, nerve, periodontal, and cardiac repair, but comparisons remain limited by inconsistent secretome preparation, dose reporting, and analytical methods. Progress towards translation will require standardised characterisation of both soluble and vesicular fractions, dose normalisation to scaffold mass or area, functional potency assays, and validation in long-term, clinically relevant animal models. Together, these developments will enable more reproducible engineering of electrospun secretome-delivery systems and support their clinical translation.

title: Clinical Considerations With GLP-1 Therapies for Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis: A Focus on Musculoskeletal Health and Nutritional Concerns.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) therapies and other incretin mimetics represent an important advance in obesity management that could potentially alter the trajectory of knee osteoarthritis (OA) incidence and management approaches. However, enthusiasm should be balanced by awareness about inadvertent musculoskeletal consequences and nutritional considerations.
DESIGN AND RESULTS: This narrative review explores evidence on implications of weight loss on muscle and bone health and malnutrition risk in the context of knee OA. Relevant literature was identified through targeted PubMed searches with emphasis on research gaps and clinical uncertainties. We examine clinical considerations for patient-centered GLP-1 therapy use and recommendations for strategies to optimize nutrition and musculoskeletal health alongside GLP-1 therapies for knee OA management.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The success of GLP-1 therapy use in knee OA management should be evaluated not by the magnitude of weight loss but by improvements in OA symptoms, physical function, body composition, musculoskeletal and cardiometabolic health, and quality of life. Optimizing outcomes will require combining pharmacotherapy with evidence-based nutrition, exercise, and long-term obesity management strategies. Further research is needed to understand how GLP-1 therapies specifically impact musculoskeletal health with knee OA, and best fit into integrated and sustainable strategies for improving joint health.

title: The 'Lower-Trap-Door' technique: Inlay trapezoidal Achilles bone-block fixation for lower trapezius tendon transfer.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe a novel inlay bone-to-bone fixation technique for lower trapezius tendon (LTT) transfer using a trapezoidal humeral osteotomy and Achilles tendon-bone allograft.
METHODS: The Lower-Trap-Door technique incorporates a wedge-shaped calcaneal bone block into a hinged trapezoidal osteotomy at the greater tuberosity. The bone block is press-fitted within the osteotomy and secured using double-row suture anchor fixation. The design creates intrinsic mechanical stability through bone-to-bone contact prior to suture compression. The technique allows integration with superior capsular reconstruction (SCR) when indicated.
RESULTS: This Technical Note details the indications, surgical setup, graft preparation, humeral osteotomy, bone-block insertion, double-row fixation, optional integration with SCR, postoperative rehabilitation, technical pearls, and potential complications. The technique has been used by the senior author in more than 15 patients, with no observed failures at the humeral bone-block interface to date. Formal clinical outcome data are not presented.
CONCLUSION: The Lower-Trap-Door technique provides an inlay bone-to-bone fixation method for LTT transfer using a trapezoidal humeral osteotomy and Achilles tendon-bone allograft. Early clinical use suggests feasibility and construct reliability at the bone-block interface, although formal biomechanical testing and prospective clinical outcome studies are required to validate its comparative effectiveness.

title: Beyond movement behaviours: Unravelling the prospective links between 24-hour behavioural composition and affective dynamics in adolescent athletes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the full spectrum of 24-h movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (SLP), screen-based sedentary behaviour (Screen-SB), light physical activity (LPA), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (S-MVPA), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (US-MVPA) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured MVPA subdomains on emotional outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). Accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. Four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (EMA): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. Bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect.
RESULTS: Associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. A higher relative proportion of LPA was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% Bayesian credible interval [CrI] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% CrI 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% CrI -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% CrI -0.236 to -0.185). In 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to LPA generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. These findings highlight LPA as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect.
CONCLUSIONS: Daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. LPA showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing SB. Promoting LPA may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands.

title: Ten Years of Training in a Male World-Class 800-1500 m Swimmer.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the training process of a world-class 800- to 1500-m swimmer and identify key characteristics and differences between successful and less successful competitive seasons.
METHODS: A mixed-methods case study design was used to capture quantitative and qualitative aspects of the training process. Data were collected through (1) 10 years of training logs (ages 19-28); (2) in-depth semistructured interviews with the swimmer, his club coach, and national team head coach; and (3) systematic quality assurance through negotiation among researchers and key informants.
RESULTS: Performance improved gradually until 23 to 24 years of age before slightly declining. Annual training volume ranged from ∼1000 to ∼1380 hours per year, with swimming accounting for ∼80% of total training time in most seasons (2700-3700 km·y-1), including extensive long-course, stroke-specific training. The swimmer followed a traditional periodization model with 3 macrocycles annually, characterized by high volumes of low-intensity training during preparation and increased intensity with reduced volume approaching competition. A later shift toward more zone 2 training at the expense of zone 1 and reduced long-course exposure coincided with the performance decline in his mid-twenties. Successful seasons were characterized by high quality in the holistic training process, including strong motivation and structured recovery, whereas less successful seasons were marked by slightly weaker recovery habits, and declining motivation and self-confidence.
CONCLUSION: This study provides novel information regarding the training process for a world-class long-distance swimmer, including differences between successful and less successful seasons. These data may serve as a framework for practitioners aiming to optimize long-term performance development.

title: Minimally Invasive Arthroscopic Repair of Medial Meniscus Ramp Lesions Without an Accessory Posteromedial Portal.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Ramp lesions are reported in approximately 15-25% of patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. Biomechanical studies have shown that untreated ramp lesions increase anterior tibial translation and internal rotation under load, whereas repair of these lesions restores knee kinematics closer to normal. Owing to the difficulty of visualizing and accessing these lesions through standard anterior arthroscopic portals, several surgical techniques advocate using an accessory posteromedial portal for adequate diagnosis and repair. Case Presentation: A 19-year-old male presented with a seven-month history of right knee pain and instability. Based on clinical examination and radiological assessment, he was diagnosed with a complete ACL tear and a medial meniscus ramp lesion involving the posterior horn meniscocapsular junction. The patient underwent successful ACL reconstruction and all-inside ramp lesion repair using only standard anterior arthroscopic portals, without posteromedial exploration. Adequate visualization through the anterolateral portal, appropriate knee positioning during repair, and careful control of the depth of the repair device were key factors in achieving reduction and fixation. The procedure was well tolerated, and postoperative recovery was uneventful. The patient was followed regularly in the clinic for two years. A supervised physiotherapy program was initiated, and he successfully returned to daily activities and sport without limitations. Conclusions: This case highlights the feasibility of repairing medial meniscus ramp lesions through standard anterior arthroscopic portals without an accessory posteromedial portal. This approach may offer an alternative surgical option in selected cases.

title: Can Standardized Small-Sided Games Be Used as a Tool to Monitor Post-Match Fatigue in Male Academy Soccer Players?
abstract: This study aimed to analyze residual post-match fatigue using time-motion analysis across small-sided games (SSGs), fitness performance, and heart rate variability (HRV) in academy soccer players. Fifteen male academy players (18.3 ± 0.6 years) performed four SSG formats: 3 vs. 3 and 3 vs. 3 + 2 goalkeepers, played on small (25 × 18 m; 75 m2 per player) and large (36 × 25 m; 150 m2 per player) areas in a four-week experimental design. Two non-match weeks served as baseline weeks, and two weeks followed an official match. Time-motion during SSGs was monitored via GNSS. Before each training session (24, 72, and 120 h post-match), HRV, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, and maximum isometric force (MIF) of the hamstrings were measured. External load metrics were generally lower in post-match sessions than in non-match weeks; however, their low reliability limited the interpretability of SSG outputs. CMJ height was reduced, MIF was elevated post-match, whereas HRV showed distinct mid-week responses, decreasing in starters but increasing in non-starters. Post-match fatigue was evident in neuromuscular performance but was inconsistently reflected in SSG outputs. CMJ height reliably reflects post-match fatigue in male academy soccer players and should be prioritized when monitoring neuromuscular recovery.

title: Unilateral Versus Bilateral Squat Velocity-Based Training in Recreationally Trained Men: Effects of a 6-Week Intervention on Strength, Jump, and Sprint Performance.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The main aim was to analyze the effect of bilateral and unilateral squat velocity-based training on strength, jump, sprint, and change-of-direction (COD) performance.
METHODS: Twenty recreationally trained men (age: 23.1 ± 5.5 y) were randomly assigned to bilateral (n = 9) or unilateral (n = 11) squat training groups and followed a 6-week velocity-based training intervention using the bilateral or the unilateral squat exercise, respectively. Pre- and posttraining measurements included: modified 505 COD test with each leg; linear 20-m sprint; countermovement jump and broad jump, evaluated under both bilateral and unilateral conditions; and incremental loading tests in the bilateral and unilateral squat exercises.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions favoring unilateral squat training group were observed for right-leg unilateral broad jump and COD (P ≤ .05). Significant main effects of time were observed for bilateral and unilateral countermovement jump performance and squat velocity variables (P < .05), with no significant group × time interactions. No significant changes were observed in sprint performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Both bilateral and unilateral squat velocity-based training effectively improved vertical jump performance and movement velocity in squat exercises. However, unilateral training produced greater improvements in unilateral performance tasks, particularly in the broad jump and COD with the right leg. These findings suggest that while both approaches enhance general neuromuscular performance, unilateral squat training may provide additional benefits for unilateral explosive actions without producing superior adaptations in sprint performance.

title: Bilateral insufficiency fractures of the femoral condyles after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy for ulcerative colitis: A case report.
abstract: Glucocorticoid therapy is a well-established risk factor for osteoporosis and insufficiency fractures. However, insufficiency fractures developing after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy have been infrequently described. We present a case of bilateral insufficiency fractures of the femoral condyles detected approximately one year after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy in a patient with ulcerative colitis. A 53-year-old man presented with progressive bilateral knee pain without antecedent trauma. He had previously received glucocorticoid therapy for ulcerative colitis, including oral prednisolone and budesonide. The last course had been discontinued approximately one year before symptom onset. Physical examination revealed bilateral weight-bearing pain with mild swelling but without redness or restriction of motion. Laboratory findings showed no inflammatory response, and plain X-rays showed no abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed bilateral bone marrow edema and fracture lines in the femoral condyles, consistent with bilateral insufficiency fractures. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry confirmed osteoporosis, with T-scores of -2.4 at the lumbar spine and -3.3 at the femoral neck, and trabecular bone score was 1.171, suggesting that the trabecular microarchitecture was markedly degraded. He was treated with temporary non-weight-bearing rehabilitation and daily administration of abaloparatide. Knee pain gradually improved, and follow-up magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated resolution of signal abnormalities. Bone mineral density showed modest improvement, although trabecular bone score remained in the degraded range. In patients with a history of glucocorticoid exposure, bone fragility persists even after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy, and ongoing evaluation and treatment for osteoporosis are necessary.

title: 4-Mercaptoethyl-Pyridine-Functionalized EAK Peptide Hydrogel Prolongs Intra-Articular Retention of Infliximab and Modulates Cartilage Fibrosis-Related Readouts in Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degeneration and inflammatory microenvironment dysregulation. TNF-α-associated inflammatory and fibrotic changes, together with declining endogenous repair capacity during OA progression, have been implicated in the pathological remodeling of OA, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that address both inflammatory and regenerative challenges. TNF-α-targeting biologics provide a potential means of modulating inflammatory signaling but may exhibit limited intra-articular retention. Here, we developed a 4-mercaptoethyl-pyridine (MEP)-functionalized EAK peptide hydrogel (IFX@AP) as a common delivery platform for infliximab (IFX) for stage-informed therapeutic intervention in OA. This tailor-made EAK-GSG-MEP hydrogel exhibited affinity-associated retention of the antibody within the peptide network. In the 2-week post-anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) intervention setting, IFX@AP was associated with reduced TNF-α immunoreactivity and attenuated cartilage fibrosis. In the 4-week post-ACLT intervention setting, IFX@AP was further combined with adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADMSCs). IFX@AP improved adhesion-associated behavior of ADMSCs, enhanced their viability in vitro, and prolonged their joint-associated fluorescence retention after ACLT, thereby promoting OA repair. In summary, this MEP-functionalized peptide hydrogel provides a common delivery platform that can be readily adapted to different therapeutic regimens and may support stage-informed approaches to OA management.

title: Gender Differences in Sports Injuries of the Foot and Ankle.
abstract: This article examines sex-based differences in foot and ankle injuries among female athletes, emphasizing the role of anatomic, hormonal, biomechanical, and sociocultural factors. Female athletes are disproportionately affected by ankle sprains, chronic instability, and bone stress injuries. Conditions such as relative energy deficiency in sport and the female athlete triad contribute to injury risk and long-term health consequences but remain under-recognized. This article highlights disparities in research, treatment, and outcomes, calling for improved screening, sex-specific prevention strategies, and greater inclusion of female subjects in sports medicine research to inform evidence-based care and optimize outcomes for female athletes.

title: Understanding Sleep in Ultramarathon Runners: An Exploratory Assessment during a Training Week.
abstract: Sleep plays a vital role in sports performance. Ultramarathon runners may experience impaired sleep during training and competition; however, further investigation is needed. The current study aimed to evaluate sleep in ultramarathon runners during a typical training week. We evaluated 15 male athletes with a mean age of 45.1 ± 10.5 years and a mean ultramarathon experience of 6.37 ± 6.49 years. Sleep was assessed using the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire, the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Athlete Sleep Behavior Questionnaire, the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and a 7-day sleep diary. Most participants were morning chronotypes (86.7%), and the mean social jetlag of was 0.60 ± 0.69 hour. The athletes went to bed and woke up earlier on workdays than on free days ( p = 0.002). Most athletes reported < 8 hours of sleep per night, 53.3% reported poor sleep-related behaviors, and 46.7% were classified as poor sleepers; however, 73.3% did not report excessive daytime sleepiness. These findings suggest a heterogeneous and multidimensional sleep-health profile in ultramarathon runners.

title: Voluntary wheel running attenuates mechanical hypersensitivity but transiently prolongs gait impairments in male and female mice with unilateral osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Physical activity is a first-line therapeutic intervention for managing osteoarthritis-related pain and functional impairment. However, the growing literature questions the long-term relevance of exercise-induced improvements in patients, while pre-clinical research evidence-base is limited by reliance on stressful, forced exercise paradigms which do not reflect voluntary engagement. Here, we investigated the effects of voluntary wheel running on the pain experience in mice with joint pain.
DESIGN: We investigated the impact of free access to a running wheel on sensory, functional and affective outcomes following unilateral intra-articular injection of monoiodoacetate (MIA) into the knee joint of 8-week-old male and female C57Bl/6J mice (n=14/16). Mice were single-housed and randomly assigned to remain sedentary or have unrestricted access to a wheel from at least two weeks before MIA. Behavioural outcomes were assessed longitudinally over an eight-week post-injection period.
RESULTS: Mean daily running distance decreased from 3.01 to 0.69 km in males and from 3.90 to 1.69 km in females by day 5 after MIA. Following a short-lived recovery, males showed a progressive decline, while the rebound in activity was sustained in females throughout the observation period. Voluntary wheel running attenuated MIA-induced secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, with higher mechanical withdrawal thresholds in active than sedentary mice, most obviously during the pain-like maintenance stage (day 40: males: 0.08g; 95%CI 0.040 to 0.126; females: 0.125g, 95%CI 0.029 to 0.222). Conversely, wheel running transiently delayed full gait recovery, with between-group differences in stance symmetry and duty factor during early recovery in both sexes (males day 20: stance: -11.8%; 95%CI -21.25 to -2.27; duty factor: -5.4%; 95%CI -10.53 to -0.35; females day 12: stance: -22.0%; 95%CI -32.48 to -11.51; duty factor: -15.9%; 95%CI -22.97 to -8.83). Finally, wheel access had little effect on anxio-depressive-like behaviours or cognition, but reduced faecal output and influenced body weight.
CONCLUSIONS: In this animal model of MIA-induced osteoarthritis, voluntary wheel running was associated with improvements in secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, despite a transient and acute worsening of several gait impairments. These findings highlight the importance of assessing multiple behavioural domains in preclinical studies and underscore the complexity of exercise-induced effects on pain and function.

title: Subscapularis Rotator Cuff Repair: Technique and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Subscapularis tendon pathology has transitioned from a historically underrecognized entity to a critical focus of modern shoulder surgery. Contemporary advances in imaging, arthroscopic visualization, and biomechanical understanding have significantly improved detection and treatment of subscapularis tears. The tendon plays a central role in anterior glenohumeral stability and maintenance of the glenohumeral force couple. Tears frequently involve the superior border and rotator interval complex and are often associated with biceps instability. Diagnosis requires integration of a thorough history, physical examination maneuvers, imaging findings, and dynamic intraoperative assessment. Arthroscopic repair strategies include single-row, double-row, modified Mason-Allen, and knotless constructs, with clinical outcomes demonstrating reliable improvement across techniques. It is important to review the historical context, anatomy, classification, diagnostic evaluation, surgical technique, repair constructs, outcomes, rehabilitation, complications, and emerging biomechanical considerations relevant to contemporary subscapularis repair.

title: Long-Term, Multimodal Chiropractic Care and Outcome Tracking in a Competitive Endurance Athlete With Chronic Neck and Low Back Pain: A Case Report.
abstract: A 51-year-old male IT executive and competitive endurance athlete (cyclist and half-Ironman competitor) presented with a six-month history of daily chronic neck pain associated with restricted cervical range of motion and episodic low back pain described as a compression sensation. Symptoms had a gradual onset, with no identifiable inciting injury. Postural examination revealed forward head posture, a left-high shoulder, upper thoracic kyphosis, and anterior pelvic tilt. Full-spine radiographs demonstrated loss of normal cervical lordosis, small osteophytes at multiple levels, and mild thoracolumbar scoliosis with degenerative facet changes. No medical diagnosis was established, as the patient was assessed and managed exclusively within a chiropractic setting. The chiropractic working impression was vertebral subluxation complex (VSC) involving the cervical, thoracic, and lumbosacral spine. The patient received chiropractic spinal adjustments, initially twice weekly and gradually tapered to approximately once weekly, over an intensive care phase of 30 visits, followed by a further course of lower-frequency maintenance care (40 cumulative visits at the last formal review, with care ongoing). Patient-rated global-change scores for neck pain, low back pain, and overall mobility indicated sustained improvement relative to the pre-care baseline, beginning at the first checkpoint and continuing through 40 visits, although some fluctuations were observed. Paraspinal thermography showed reduced cervical asymmetry at the 30-visit review, with a broadly similar lumbar pattern. In contrast, heart rate variability (HRV) parameters were paradoxically lower at the 30-visit review than at baseline, coinciding with a self-reported period of acute occupational stress preceding that recording. This case report describes patient-perceived improvement, together with qualitatively assessed improvements in range of motion, during a structured, long-term course of chiropractic care in a highly active patient exposed to cumulative mechanical loading. It also highlights the limitations of interpreting adjunctive autonomic and thermal measures in isolation from concurrent lifestyle stressors and patient-rated outcomes.

title: Chitosan hydrogels: Crosslinking mechanisms, environmental adaptability, and sports-health relevance.
abstract: The development of extreme-environment sports health interfaces is shifting from short-term signal detection toward long-term interfacial service, where the reliable performance of chitosan (CS) hydrogels depends on maintaining interfacial coupling, signal transduction, and biological function under low-temperature exposure, immersion, salt-rich sweat, and dynamic wound conditions. The protonatable amino groups of CS chains serve as crosslinking sites, cationic interfacial moieties, and structural contributors to antibacterial and hemostatic activity, while hydroxyl-mediated hydration, dynamic networks, and multicomponent modification support wet adhesion, deformation recovery, and tissue repair. In winter sports, underwater and sweat-rich exercise, and sports-related wound management, the bottleneck is not a single deficiency in mechanics, conductivity, or adhesion, but coupled failure: salt-rich sweat and immersion induce charge screening, low-temperature exposure and osmotic stress disturb hydrated networks, and repeated deformation drives conductive/adhesive pathway reconstruction, leading to signal drift and impaired repair. This review summarizes chemical and physical crosslinking strategies for CS hydrogels, clarifies the roles of carbon-based materials, metal/metal-oxide nanocomponents, and natural biomacromolecules in conductive pathway formation, network reinforcement, wet interfacial regulation, and bioactive repair, and discusses environmental adaptability and sports applications. Future directions toward long-term stability, multifunctional integration, standardized evaluation, and service reliability under realistic use conditions are proposed.

title: The Repeated Bout Effect in Young and Older Adults: Mechanisms, Age-Related Differences and Clinical Implications.
abstract: The repeated bout effect (RBE) describes the protective adaptation whereby a single bout of eccentric exercise confers resistance against muscle damage from subsequent bouts of the same or similar exercise. While the RBE is robustly documented in young adults, direct age-comparative human evidence remains limited to few small studies with predominantly male samples, and whether aging independently attenuates the RBE remains uncertain. This narrative review synthesizes the current literature on the RBE across the lifespan, with particular focus on comparisons between young and older populations. We examine the proposed mechanisms underlying the RBE-including neural, mechanical/structural, and cellular/molecular adaptations-and consider how age-related changes in skeletal muscle physiology may modify these responses. Human studies indicate that older adults can express an RBE, while preclinical evidence in aged female mice suggests reduced adaptation to repeated eccentric loading; however, smaller first-bout responses in several human comparisons complicate interpretation of an independent age effect. Proposed age-related explanations involving inflammatory signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, neural adaptations, and regenerative processes should therefore be considered hypotheses rather than established mechanisms. We conclude by identifying critical gaps in the literature and proposing future research directions to optimize eccentric exercise interventions for older adults. For practice, current evidence supports gradual introduction and individualized progression of eccentric resistance exercise, while no age-specific optimal inter-bout interval has been established.

title: Heart-to-Muscle Signaling in Heart Failure: Which Catabolic Mediators Are Truly Cardiac-Derived?
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is frequently accompanied by skeletal muscle wasting, which is present in about one in five ambulatory patients and linked to reduced exercise capacity. It is traditionally viewed as secondary to hypoperfusion, inactivity, and inflammation, yet circulating mediators rising with myocardial stress also act on muscle, and some are released by the stressed heart. We examine heart-to-muscle signaling as a directional axis, distinguishing mediators whose circulating pool is demonstrably cardiac from those for which a cardiac contribution to the circulating pool is unproven or unquantified. Across five soluble mediators (growth differentiation factor 15, fibroblast growth factor 21, myostatin, angiotensin II and activin A) and cardiac extracellular vesicles, cardiac-specific loss- and gain-of-function evidence exists only for myostatin; for growth differentiation factor 15 and fibroblast growth factor 21, a dominant cardiac contribution to the circulating pool is unproven, so the axis is better termed cardiac-stress-associated than cardiac-derived. We link each mediator to the muscle phenotype and to therapies in trials, and define the arteriovenous-sampling and cardiac loss-of-function experiments needed before the axis can be considered a validated therapeutic target.

title: Gene amplification during differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells towards chondrocytes.
abstract: For decades, gene amplification was described as an attribute of tumor cells and as a physiological mechanism to increase gene copy numbers for the higher protein demand during the development of amphibians and flies. Notably, gene amplification has since been detected in normal mammalian cells during differentiation. Numerous amplified genes detected in tumor cells overlap with amplified genes detected during stem cell differentiation. Since stem cells have a valuable potency in regenerative therapies and since cartilage regeneration is a highly demanded therapeutic strategy, the current study investigated gene amplification dynamics during the chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Using quantitative PCR, copy number changes were analyzed for genes previously implicated in differentiation, as well as genes amplified in chondrosarcoma, including CDK4, MDM2, AGAP2, CPT1B, SHANK3, TRIB1 and MYC. Amplifications were transient and stage-specific: CDK4, CPT1B and SHANK3 exhibited the highest copy number increases at day 2, followed by a gradual decline by day 7, whereas AGAP2 and MDM2 increased later in differentiation. Laser microdissection of toluidine blue-stained areas revealed heterogeneity in amplification patterns: CDK4 amplification was prominent in areas lacking or showing moderate proteoglycan deposition; CPT1B amplification occurred in regions with absent, moderate or intense proteoglycan deposition; and SHANK3 amplification was restricted to areas with intense proteoglycan deposition. Notably, regions with the strongest proteoglycan staining exhibited no gene amplification, suggesting that gene amplification is an early, transient event that diminishes as differentiation progresses. These findings highlight gene amplification as a mechanism during chondrogenesis, potentially critical for early differentiation stages and genome stability in mature cells.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded.
RESULTS: There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4).
CONCLUSION: We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Acute lower leg compartment syndrome as a result of calf strain due to a skiing injury.
abstract: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) of the lower leg is a limb-threatening condition that requires urgent management. It is most commonly caused by direct trauma, such as high-speed motor vehicle accidents or blunt force injuries, including those seen in earthquake victims. Lower extremity ACS most commonly occurs in the setting of a tibial fracture. ACS can also occur as a result of non-contact injuries, such as muscle strain during athletic activities. Early clinical suspicion and close monitoring are critical, as the most telling symptom is pain. Neurovascular signs typically appear later in the progression of the condition. While imaging tools like ultrasound and MRI may help identify muscle tears and large haematomas, they are not diagnostic for ACS. When the clinical picture is unclear, compartment pressure measurement can aid diagnosis—particularly in settings where access to surgical intervention is limited and transportation decisions are challenging. We present an unusual case of ACS in the leg following a muscle injury sustained during skiing. The patient’s severe pain, along with physical findings of increased calf diameter and ultrasound-confirmed haematoma, was a key factor prompting transfer to a higher-level care facility for urgent fasciotomy.

title: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats is partially mediated by enhancing necroptosis via phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study links Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1)-sensitive receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-associated signaling with biochemical, histological, inflammatory, and functional outcomes after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. Nec-1 reduced RIPK1 and MLKL phosphorylation, muscle injury, and early functional impairment. These findings extend prior skeletal-muscle studies by integrating molecular pathway activation with longitudinal functional recovery while supporting a contribution of RIPK1-associated necroptotic signaling.

title: Ethanol-induced alterations in mesenchymal stromal cells and the effects of aspalathin: implications for alcohol-associated osteonecrosis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol-associated osteonecrosis is a debilitating condition characterized by progressive bone destruction. Although mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) play a critical role in tissue repair, the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on MSCs and their responsiveness to microenvironmental signals remain unclear.
METHODS: MSCs were exposed to ethanol (EtOH) to evaluate changes in viable cell number, ROS-related fluorescence signals, and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. CXCL12 expression was examined in human femoral head specimens and ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. The effects of aspalathin (ASP) on EtOH-induced alterations in MSCs were also investigated.
RESULTS: EtOH exposure reduced viable MSC number and increased ROS-related fluorescence signals. It was also associated with decreased expression of ATP5A and CXCR4 and increased expression of p16. CXCL12 expression was higher in alcohol-associated osteonecrosis tissue than in osteoarthritis tissue and appeared qualitatively increased in ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. These findings indicate altered CXCL12 and CXCR4 expression across the tissue and in vitro experimental settings. ASP treatment attenuated the EtOH-induced reduction in the CCK-8 signal, was associated with attenuation of ROS-related fluorescence signals, significantly restored ATP5A expression, suppressed p16 expression, and showed a non-significant trend toward recovery of CXCR4 expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethanol exposure was associated with alterations in the cellular state of MSCs, accompanied by changes in ROS-related fluorescence signals and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. ASP partially attenuated some of these ethanol-induced alterations. Further studies are required to clarify the functional significance of these findings and to validate them in vivo.

title: Mechanically-guided mesenchymal stem cell differentiation: a promising biophysical strategy for orthopedic regeneration.
abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders often leave bone and cartilage incompletely restored. Mesenchymal stem cells offer regenerative potential, but their fate is strongly shaped by mechanical context. In this Review, we examine how tensile strain, compression, fluid shear, hydrostatic pressure and matrix mechanics are converted into signals that influence bone- and cartilage-forming programmes. We highlight how cell source, donor variability, loading dose and timing, three-dimensional culture and scaffold properties shape these responses, and discuss the barriers to translating mechanically guided strategies into reproducible, safe approaches for bone and cartilage regeneration.

title: Tarsometatarsal Joint Synovial Chondromatosis Requiring Osteotomy-Assisted Tumor Excision With Staged Revision for Nonunion: A Case Report.
abstract: Synovial chondromatosis (SC) is a rare benign proliferative disorder characterized by chondroid metaplasia of the synovial membrane that most commonly affects large joints; foot and ankle involvement is exceedingly rare. This case report describes SC involving the fourth tarsometatarsal joint with deep plantar extension between the third and fourth metatarsal bases in a 41-year-old woman. Magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography demonstrated a complex soft tissue mass with adjacent bony erosion, and image-guided core needle biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. Given the deep plantar extent of the lesion precluding standard dorsal excision, a combined orthopaedic foot and ankle and orthopaedic oncology approach was undertaken. The approach utilized a novel fourth metatarsal base osteotomy with temporary complete bone removal to achieve full tumor exposure and complete gross excision. The osteotomy subsequently progressed to nonunion, requiring staged revision with iliac crest bone grafting, bone marrow aspirate concentrate injection, and revision low-profile fixation. At 4 months postrevision, the patient reported walking normally with radiographic confirmation of osteotomy healing. This case highlights a novel surgical approach for deeply located SC of the midfoot and underscores the value of multidisciplinary planning for complex benign foot tumors.Level of Evidence:Level V-Expert Opinion/Case Report.

title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.

title: Metabolic Bone Health in Female Patients: Focus on Foot and Ankle.
abstract: Metabolic bone health is crucial for the overall well-being of female patients. Female athletes and young females are of particular interest, as their skeletal systems are still developing and are sensitive to the hormonal and physical stress of training and diet. Stress fractures occur with higher frequency in females with risk factors such as low bone mineral density (BMD). When low bone mineral density occurs along with menstrual irregularities and relative energy deficiency, it completes the female triad (23, 27, and 28). Any discussion of female BMD and metabolic bone health must include the female triad.

title: Analytical strategies for distinguishing endogenous and exogenous anabolic androgenic steroids in doping control.
abstract: Doping control for anabolic androgenic steroids (AASs) must separate endogenous physiology from exogenous administration when the same molecular entities occur on both sides of the boundary. This Critical Review evaluates analytical strategies for that source-attribution problem, with emphasis on urinary steroid profiling, longitudinal interpretation, compound-specific isotope ratio mass spectrometry, intact phase-II metabolites, alternative matrices, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and data-driven evidence integration. Current practice relies on a staged logic: routine steroid-profile measurements define marker behavior, the steroidal module of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) evaluates individual changes, and gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry (GC-C-IRMS) supplies orthogonal source evidence when pseudo-endogenous steroids or atypical profiles require confirmation. UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B17 (UGT2B17) deletion, sex, menstrual-cycle phase, pregnancy, medication, and sample degradation can alter marker concentrations and ratios. Intact conjugates, dried blood spots (DBS), HRMS metabolite discovery, and statistical tools can provide additional evidence, but their performance depends on validation for the relevant matrix and administration scenario. The most defensible strategy is therefore a tiered framework that combines longitudinal interpretation, source-specific chemical evidence, and expert review.

title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis.
abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

title: Age-Dependent Alterations in Glutathione Metabolites Following Muscle Injury.
abstract: Age-related impairments in antioxidant defences contribute to delayed tissue repair and increased susceptibility to oxidative stress following muscle injury. Glutathione (GSH), a key cellular antioxidant, plays a central role in redox homeostasis and recovery processes. GSH is synthesized through a sequential process involving glutamic acid and cysteine, catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to form γ-glutamyl cysteine (γGC), which subsequently combines with glycine to produce GSH. Using metabolomic profiling and acute skeletal muscle injury in mice, this study characterized age-dependent alterations in GSH biosynthesis. Clustering analysis identified that muscle from 12-month-old mice have a delayed GSH synthesis profile in response to injury compared to 3-month-old mice, with an age-dependent delay in γGC accumulation. This suggests that aging negatively influences metabolite profiles within the GSH synthesis pathway. As γGC lies downstream of this enzymatic step, its supplementation may bypass the GCL bottleneck. To test this, C2C12 myoblasts were treated with γGC (from 1-100 µg/mL), however this did not affect myoblast proliferation or differentiation. These data suggest detrimental age-related dysregulation of GSH-related metabolites in skeletal muscle repair, particularly γGC, however further examination of the role of exogenous γGC supplementation in this process is required to identify further therapeutic benefit.

title: Evaluation of a four-herb Chinese medicine formula at different concentrations on muscle damage and inflammation in a rat model of DOMS.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) impairs exercise recovery, while current treatments remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas may provide safe, multi-target interventions.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the dose-dependent protective effects of a four-herb Chinese medicine formulation (safflower, Chinese Angelica, peach kernel and myrrh) against DOMS in a rat model.
METHODS: Thirty-two male SPF SD rats were randomly allocated to control or low- (1696 mg/kg), medium- (3392 mg/kg), or high-dose (6784 mg/kg) groups. The formulation was administered orally for 11 days, with DOMS induced by exhaustive swimming on day 8. Serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 were measured at baseline and at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h post-exercise.
RESULTS: The medium- and high-dose groups exhibited significantly lower serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 levels than controls, with the high-dose group showing the largest reductions. The low-dose group showed limited or no significant reductions in most markers, demonstrating a clear dose-dependent protective effect.
CONCLUSIONS: The formulation dose-dependently attenuates muscle damage and inflammation in a rat DOMS model, with high-dose treatment achieving the fastest recovery. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm the efficacy and safety in humans.

title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

title: Moderate-intensity exercise attenuates osteoarthritis progression by inhibiting cellular inflammation and apoptosis via the TRPV1-mediated NLRP3 inflammatory pathway.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is characterized by progressive joint degeneration driven in part by inflammatory and mechanical stress-responsive pathways. This study investigated whether the protective effects of moderate-intensity exercise are mediated through the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1)-NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome axis. OA was induced in mice by destabilization of the medial meniscus, followed by low-, moderate-, or high-intensity treadmill exercise. Joint pathology was evaluated histologically, and TRPV1 function was examined using gain- and loss-of-function approaches in vitro and in vivo. Moderate-intensity exercise reduced cartilage degeneration, synovitis, subchondral bone remodeling, and chondrocyte apoptosis, whereas high-intensity exercise was associated with more severe joint pathology. TRPV1 and NLRP3 expression were suppressed by moderate exercise but increased with greater cyclic mechanical strain in primary chondrocytes. TRPV1 overexpression enhanced NLRP3 signaling, inflammatory cytokine release, caspase-1 activation, and apoptosis, while TRPV1 knockdown produced the opposite effects. Pharmacological inhibition of NLRP3 attenuated the detrimental effects of TRPV1 overexpression. These findings identify TRPV1-NLRP3 signaling as a mechanosensitive pathway linking exercise intensity to OA progression and suggest that moderate mechanical loading protects the joint by suppressing this axis.

title: First-in-human quantitative magnetic particle imaging maps in vivo intra-articular mesenchymal stromal cell kinetics in knee osteoarthritis.
abstract: The clinical translation of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is limited by the absence of a noninvasive method to quantify aspects of intra-articular cell fate through longitudinal tracking of cell-associated tracer kinetics after administration. Here, we report the first-in-human application of quantitative magnetic particle imaging (MPI) for in vivo tracking of intra-articular MSCs. Clinical-grade human umbilical cord-derived MSCs were labeled with ferumoxytol and monitored using open-geometry MPI platforms that enabled both volumetric imaging and bedside regional mapping. In vitro studies showed a strong linear correlation between MPI signal and labeled cell number, supporting quantitative analysis. In a patient with KOA, serial imaging over 10 days demonstrated rapid redistribution of cell-associated signal from the injection site into distinct joint compartments, followed by progressive decline consistent with dynamic post-injection clearance. In an osteoarthritis mouse model, longitudinal MPI kinetics were corroborated by histological detection of the iron label within joint tissues and were associated with reduced cartilage degeneration. Together, these findings establish open-geometry MPI as a clinically practical platform for quantitative cell tracking after local administration. This approach provides a measurable delivery-exposure framework for evaluating cell retention, regional redistribution, and signal persistence, and may help guide dose selection, administration strategies, and treatment optimization for regenerative therapies in osteoarthritis.

title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model.
abstract: Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80-200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

title: Single-Cell Atlas of Embryonic Fibroblasts and the Nanog-id4 Regulatory Axis in Chinese Soft-Shelled Turtle (Pelodiscus sinensis).
abstract: Embryonic fibroblasts serve as crucial mesenchymal progenitors during vertebrate organogenesis, yet their heterogeneity, developmental trajectories and regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood in non-mammalian species, including Pelodiscus sinensis, a pivotal model for studies on animals' evolutionary adaptation and embryonic development. Here we established an in vitro culture system for embryonic fibroblasts from P. sinensis and characterised their transcript identity, differentiation potential and response to pluripotency factor Nanog. Through single-cell transcriptomic profiling of embryonic stages E0, E3 and E5, we identified a putative fibroblast population that is classified into six transcriptionally distinct subclusters along a bifurcating pseudotime trajectory, with mesenchymal stem cells serving as the root progenitor giving rise to proliferating mesenchyme, neural crest-like mesenchyme and smooth muscle lineages. Additionally, we demonstrated that adenoviral-mediated overexpression of nanog in cultured fibroblasts markedly enhances cell proliferation and found that the ALP-positive staining area increased and the transcripts of pluripotency-associated genes including sox2, lin28a and id4 were upregulated. Particularly, CUT&RUN assays demonstrated Nanog occupancy at two putative binding sites within the id4 promoter, supporting it as a candidate direct target. Collectively, our findings uncover the developmental heterogeneity of turtle embryonic fibroblasts, defining Nanog as a regulator of stemness-associated phenotypes and proliferation, and provide evidence for a regulatory link between Nanog and downstream effectors. This work established a reptilian fibroblast model for studying mesenchymal plasticity and offered mechanistic insights that may inform regenerative strategies across vertebrates.
